findings.title: Optimized audit-log path returns 500 for any non-empty result set
findings.description:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` copies the numeric key logic from `Paginator`: `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The endpoint orders by `-datetime`, and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `models.DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. On the first page `cursor.value` is 0, so `_build_next_values` calls `key(results[0])` whenever there is at least one row (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122). A request with `?optimized_pagination=true` from an admin or global-access member therefore 500s whenever the org has audit entries. Only empty result sets succeed.

`value_from_cursor` (paginator.py:842-843) also returns the raw cursor integer. `DateTimePaginator` (paginator.py:238-241) converts the millisecond value back to a datetime, and this class does not. Even after fixing the key, `build_queryset`'s `col >= %s` would compare a datetime column to an int. Subclassing `DateTimePaginator` would fix both. No test covers this path (see the test-debt finding).

findings.title: Audit-log GET raises AttributeError for API-key callers without membership
findings.description:
`enable_advanced` is computed on every request, before the `use_optimized` check. It dereferences `organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:346). `convert_args` looks up the org with `user_id=request.user.id` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:285-291), so `member` is `None` for principals without membership. API-key requests authenticate as `AnonymousUser()` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:518), so `is_superuser` is false and the `or` falls through to `None.has_global_access`. `OrganizationAuditPermission` admits such a key when it carries `org:write` (src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:110-124). The result is an AttributeError and a 500 on every audit-log GET from that key, even without `optimized_pagination`.

Fix: evaluate the check only inside the optimized condition and guard the `None` case, e.g. `use_optimized and (request.user.is_superuser or (organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access))`.

findings.title: Span-buffer key type changes from SET to ZSET with no migration or key rename
findings.description:
The `span-buf:s:{…}` keys switch from SET (`sadd`, `scard`, `sunionstore`, `sscan`) to ZSET (`zadd`, `zcard`, `zunionstore`, `zscan`) in `process_spans` (buffer.py:196-199), `_load_segment_data` (buffer.py:434-449), and add-buffer.lua:46-59. The key names are unchanged. Keys written by the old code stay in Redis for up to `redis_ttl` (3600s, buffer.py:151), and the Lua `expire` refreshes that TTL on each write (add-buffer.lua:56). Commands from the new code on those SET keys return WRONGTYPE: `ZADD` in `process_spans`, `ZCARD` and `ZUNIONSTORE` in the script, and `ZSCAN` during flush. The pipelines raise, so the consumer errors until the old keys expire.

Fix: give the ZSET format a new prefix (e.g. `span-buf:z:`), or drain the buffer as part of the deploy. The module docstring glossary (buffer.py:58, 61) still describes these as set keys.

findings.title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated
findings.description: `zpopmin` drops the lowest-scored spans whenever a segment exceeds 1000, and nothing is emitted. The removed Python guard in `_load_segment_data` logged `logger.error` and incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` before skipping the segment. Data loss is now harder to see than before. Emit a metric (and ideally a log line) when `span_count > 1000`.

findings.title: `max_segment_spans` is dead, and the span limit is defined in two places
findings.description: After the span-count check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, `max_segment_spans` is still accepted by `SpansBuffer.__init__` (buffer.py:150) and stored (buffer.py:158), but nothing reads it. The effective limit is the hardcoded `1000` in add-buffer.lua:62-63, and the Python default is `1001`. Remove the parameter, or pass the limit to the script as an ARGV so there is one source of truth.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets are clamped or crash, contrary to the comments
findings.description: The comment says negative offsets are "allowed," but the new line does something else. For next cursors, `max(0, offset)` silently clamps a negative offset to 0. Before this change Django raised, so a failed request now returns 200 with the wrong page. `build_cursor` still derives the next offset from the negative value (`next_offset = offset + limit`, src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:141), so the next request can repeat the same page. For prev cursors the offset passes through unchanged to `queryset[offset:stop]`, and Django rejects negative slice bounds, so the comment is wrong there too. `Cursor.from_string` (cursors.py:58-59) accepts a negative integer offset from any client-supplied cursor. This affects every `BasePaginator` subclass, not only audit logs. The new comment in cursors.py:26-27 also claims a change that the diff does not make. Revert this hunk and that comment unless there is a tested use case.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch in `OptimizedCursorPaginator` always errors
findings.description: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and the offset is negative, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django rejects negative slice bounds, so this branch always fails. The comments say "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "permissions are checked at the queryset level." Neither matches the code. The queryset is scoped by `organization_id`, and permissions are checked in the endpoint's permission class. Remove the branch, or implement backward pagination explicitly.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` duplicates `BasePaginator.get_result`
findings.description: About 90 lines copy `BasePaginator.get_result`. The only real difference is the negative-offset branch described above. The docstring promises "streamlined boundary condition handling" and an "optimized query path for large datasets," and neither exists. Every future pagination fix would have to be applied twice. Use a hook on `BasePaginator` (for example, a method that computes the start offset), or drop the class.

findings.title: `ZUNIONSTORE` sums scores for members present in both sources
findings.description: `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. When the same payload appears in both sources, for example a redelivered span routed into two sets, its score becomes the sum of two end timestamps. That makes it look newest to `zpopmin` and changes which spans are trimmed. Line 53 has the same issue. Pass `"AGGREGATE", "MIN"` (or `MAX`, chosen deliberately) in both calls. Scores are otherwise unused, so the impact is limited to trim order.

findings.title: New behavior is untested
findings.description: The test diffs only add an `end_timestamp_precise=` argument to existing span-buffer fixtures. Nothing tests `optimized_pagination=true`, which is the path that fails above. Nothing tests an API-key or no-membership caller, negative cursor offsets, the 1000-span trim, duplicate-member score aggregation, or the new redirect depth limit in tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py. The existing `test_superuser_read_write_can_see_audit_logs` (lines 183-198) passes only because `is_superuser` short-circuits before `member` is read.

findings.title: Lint and formatting violations
findings.description: There are three blank lines before `class OptimizedCursorPaginator` (E303). Trailing whitespace appears at paginator.py:824, 827, and 829, and at organization_auditlogs.py:72 and 89. Run `ruff format` or the pre-commit hooks before merge.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit lowered without mention
findings.description: The loop bound changed from `10000` to `1000`, and the comment about the depth limit was removed. Redirect chains deeper than 1000 are now left unresolved, which can place their spans in a different set than the root's. If the change is intended, keep a comment that states the limit.
